audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-008: Is RANDOM_CHALLENGE_KZG_CELL_BATCH_DOMAIN globally unique and collision-free across all protocol contexts?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: The domain separator RANDOM_CHALLENGE_KZG_CELL_BATCH_DOMAIN is defined as the static C string literal "RCKZGCBATCH__V1_" (16 bytes) in the c-kzg-4844 C library (eip7594.c). The Go layer passes bytes directly through to ckzg4844.VerifyCellKZGProofBatch without modification. No abstract domain anomaly in the Go wrapper.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: Collision enumeration: EIP-4844 blob batch domain is "RCKZGBATCH___V1_" (three underscores, no C) byte-distinct from "RCKZGCBATCH__V1_". BLS consensus domains are 4-byte little-endian uint32 values incompatible format entirely. No collision path exists.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: A cross-protocol attack requires an exact domain byte collision. The domain is non-configurable, protected by a compile-time length assertion. No configuration or code path allows substitution.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: Specification compliance confirmed: the spec specifies RANDOM_CHALLENGE_KZG_CELL_BATCH_DOMAIN = b'RCKZGCBATCH__V1_' matching the C implementation byte-for-byte. The constant is hardcoded and cannot be weakened by attacker input.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_identified: Hardcoded constant with compile-time length assertion in c-kzg-4844

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: The domain separator is a well-defined constant with documented uniqueness rationale; it is byte-distinct from all other Ethereum protocol domain separators enumerated. No collision risk exists.

audit_items.summary: RANDOM_CHALLENGE_KZG_CELL_BATCH_DOMAIN ("RCKZGCBATCH__V1_") is globally unique, non-configurable, byte-distinct from all other Ethereum domain separators, and protected by a compile-time length assertion. No domain collision vulnerability exists.

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Does P2P gossip validation reject proofs generated with foreign domain separators?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: The P2P gossip validation path is: validateDataColumn -> validateWithKzgBatchVerifier -> verifyKzgBatch -> peerdas.VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs -> kzg.VerifyCellKZGProofBatch -> ckzg4844.VerifyCellKZGProofBatch. The C library independently recomputes the Fiat-Shamir challenge using the hardcoded domain. No foreign domain can be injected at the Go layer.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: A mismatched domain produces a distinct challenge scalar inside the C library, causing the pairing equation to fail and returning (false, nil). The Go wrapper propagates this as ErrInvalidKZGProof -> pubsub.ValidationReject. The fallback unbatched path uses the same verification function. No alternative acceptance path exists.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: Foreign-domain proofs are rejected via cryptographic pairing-check failure (not a format check), triggering ValidationReject. Sender is penalized via BadResponsesScorer. No timing oracle exposure: pairing check is constant-time in the C library.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: Rejection invariant holds: foreign-domain proofs produce a different Fiat-Shamir challenge, causing the pairing check to fail. The Go wrapper correctly propagates both the boolean result and the error return, and the caller chain terminates with ValidationReject on any false result.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_identified: Hardcoded domain in C library; pairing failure propagated as ValidationReject

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: P2P gossip validation correctly rejects foreign-domain proofs via cryptographic failure. No bypass path exists.

audit_items.summary: Foreign-domain proofs fail KZG verification at the cryptographic level (pairing equation mismatch), are propagated as ValidationReject, and result in peer penalization. No bypass is possible.

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Do validators correctly apply domain separator before attesting to blocks with data columns?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: All data column KZG verification contexts in Prysm use a single registered verifier function peerdas.VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs. This function ultimately calls ckzg4844.VerifyCellKZGProofBatch with the hardcoded C constant domain.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: No configuration option allows substitution of an alternative verification function. The single-entry-point pattern eliminates domain divergence within Prysm. The hardcoded C constant is identical for all code paths.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: Validators use the same ckzg4844 library as the P2P layer. No divergence between gossip validation and attestation verification is possible within this client.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: Domain consistency invariant holds: all verification paths in Prysm use the same C library constant RANDOM_CHALLENGE_KZG_CELL_BATCH_DOMAIN. No divergence between validators and P2P nodes is possible within this codebase.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_identified: Single verification function registered for all contexts; hardcoded domain in C library

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: Domain separator is identical across all verification contexts within Prysm. No consensus-split risk from domain divergence in this codebase.

audit_items.summary: All Prysm verification contexts use the same peerdas.VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs -> ckzg4844.VerifyCellKZGProofBatch path with hardcoded domain. No domain divergence is possible within this client.

audit_items.title: Verify Domain Separator Construction: Is RANDOM_CHALLENGE_KZG_CELL_BATCH_DOMAIN derived using a collision-resistant method?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: The Fiat-Shamir challenge construction in eip7594.c is: SHA-256(domain_16B || FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_BLOB_8B || FIELD_ELEMENTS_PER_CELL_8B || num_commitments_8B || num_cells_8B || commitments_48B*n || commitment_indices_8B*m || cell_indices_8B*m || cells_2048B*m || proofs_48B*m). All fields are fixed-size. The domain occupies a fixed 16-byte prefix.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: The domain is not null-terminated in the hash buffer; it is protected by compile-time assertions. An additional assert verifies the complete buffer was consumed. This construction is immune to variable-length confusion and extension attacks.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: The domain is a 16-byte ASCII constant with no configurable components. No variable-length input can overlap the domain prefix due to the fixed-size field layout. Extension attacks are prevented by the buffer consumption assertion.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: Domain separator construction is cryptographically sound: it is a fixed-size constant prefix in a fixed-layout hash buffer, preventing prefix collisions, variable-length confusion, and extension attacks.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_identified: Fixed-size domain prefix + buffer length assertion in c-kzg-4844

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: Domain separator construction is cryptographically sound with fixed-size fields, compile-time assertions, and SHA-256-based collision resistance.

audit_items.summary: RANDOM_CHALLENGE_KZG_CELL_BATCH_DOMAIN is a well-designed collision-resistant constant in a fixed-layout SHA-256 transcript. Fixed-size field structure prevents all known confusion attacks.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-008: Is hash input order in compute_verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch_challenge deterministic and canonical?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs assembles inputs by iterating sidecars in slice order, then rows within each sidecar in index order. No sorting or canonical ordering is applied before calling kzg.VerifyCellKZGProofBatch. Different input orderings yield different Fiat-Shamir challenges internally, but verification output is a boolean not a shared value.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: For all valid orderings of a fixed set of (commitment, cell_index, cell, proof) tuples, verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch returns true if each individual proof is valid. The Fiat-Shamir transform yields a sound aggregated pairing check for any linear combination challenge. No counterexample found.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: The sidecar ordering is controlled by P2P incoming gossip. An attacker could craft sidecars to influence batch ordering, but since verification is local and output is boolean, the attacker gains no advantage. Consensus only depends on the boolean outcome plus Merkle-anchored block body root.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: Invariant: VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs returns true iff all individual pairs are cryptographically valid. The c-kzg-4844 mathematical soundness guarantees this holds for any input ordering. Consensus compares block body roots, not KZG challenge scalars.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_identified: c-kzg-4844 batch verification is sound for any permutation of valid inputs; consensus depends on boolean outcome not challenge scalar

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: No consensus safety vulnerability. The Fiat-Shamir challenge is internal to the local verification; different validators arrive at the same boolean result for valid data regardless of input ordering.

audit_items.summary: Hash input order is local to each validator's verification call and does not affect consensus. The batch verification is sound for any permutation of valid inputs; consensus depends on the boolean verification outcome plus block body root.

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Do validators compute identical Fiat-Shamir challenges when verifying the same data column proofs?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: Validators independently compute VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs locally; the result is a boolean not a shared challenge scalar. The Fiat-Shamir challenge r is internal to verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch and is never compared across nodes.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: No scenario exists where two validators with the same set of valid (commitment, cell_index, cell, proof) tuples but different internal ordering would disagree on the verification outcome. The c-kzg-4844 batch verification is mathematically sound for any challenge derived from permuted inputs.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: Validators share individual sidecar objects via P2P, not the result of the batch challenge computation. The hash/challenge computation path is entirely local. No cross-validator comparison of challenge values occurs.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: Validators reaching consensus compare block hash (including KZG commitments via body root Merkle tree), not KZG proof challenge values. All honest validators verifying the same commitment/cell/proof data get the same boolean outcome regardless of batch ordering.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_identified: Consensus compares block body roots not KZG challenge scalars

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: The premise is incorrect: validators do not compare Fiat-Shamir challenges; they independently verify proofs locally and compare block body roots. The verification result is a local pass/fail gate.

audit_items.summary: Validators never compare internal Fiat-Shamir challenge values across nodes; consensus is achieved by comparing Merkle-anchored block body roots. Identical boolean verification outcomes for valid proofs are guaranteed regardless of internal ordering.

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Are hash inputs canonicalized before feeding to compute_verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch_challenge?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: Commitment bytes are passed raw (48 bytes cast to kzg.Bytes48). Cell indices are sidecar.Index (uint64). Point validation via bytes_to_kzg_commitment occurs AFTER challenge computation in the C library but BEFORE the pairing check; invalid points cause error return rather than false-but-OK result.
state_anomalies_found: Non-canonical BLS point bytes are included in SHA-256 hash before being rejected by bytes_to_kzg_commitment in the C library; however this does not create an exploitable gap

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: BLS12-381 G1 point compression uniquely encodes each valid curve point. A malformed commitment causes C_KZG_BADARGS error (not false-but-OK). The SidecarInclusionProven verification step anchors commitments to the proposer-signed block body root, preventing substitution.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: The inclusion proof check (RequireSidecarInclusionProven) anchors commitments to the block body root signed by the proposer, so an attacker cannot substitute commitments without breaking the proposer signature.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: Guards are sufficient: RequireSidecarInclusionProven (Merkle-anchored to proposer-signed block) prevents commitment substitution; c-kzg-4844 internal validation rejects invalid BLS point encodings with error return. No canonicalization gap creates cross-implementation divergence.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_identified: SidecarInclusionProven (Merkle proof) + c-kzg-4844 internal point validation

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: No exploitable canonicalization gap: commitments are anchored by the inclusion proof against the proposer-signed block, precluding attacker substitution; the c-kzg-4844 library returns an error (not false) for invalid commitments.

audit_items.summary: No exploitable canonicalization gap exists. Commitments are Merkle-anchored to the proposer-signed block body (preventing substitution), and the C library returns an error (not false) for non-canonical BLS point encodings.

recommendations.description: Add explicit BLS point validity pre-check at the Go layer before calling VerifyCellKZGProofBatch to fail fast with better error messages.

audit_items.title: Verify Trust Boundary Integrity for tb-002/tb-008: Is the universal verification equation e(LL, LR) == e(RL, [1]) correctly implemented in verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch_impl?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: VerifyCellKZGProofBatch is a thin wrapper: it converts []Cell to []ckzg4844.Cell (same byte layout, safe cast) then delegates entirely to ckzg4844.VerifyCellKZGProofBatch. The pairing equation e(LL,LR)==e(RL,[1]) is implemented inside the c-kzg-4844 C library, not in the Go layer.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: The Go wrapper performs only a type cast (Cell to ckzg4844.Cell, identical underlying byte array). No counterexample possible in the Go layer; all verification logic including the pairing equation resides in the C library.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs calls kzg.VerifyCellKZGProofBatch, which calls the C library implementing EIP-7594 verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch with the standard pairing equation.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: The pairing equation implementation is entirely within the c-kzg-4844 C library. The Go code correctly passes all four parameters without modification. No invariant violations found in the Go wrapper.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_identified: ckzg4844.VerifyCellKZGProofBatch returns (bool, error); Go wrapper propagates both

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: The Go wrapper is correct. Any vulnerability in the pairing equation would be in the c-kzg-4844 C library (external dependency). No bug in scope for this codebase.

audit_items.summary: The Go wrapper correctly delegates to the c-kzg-4844 C library with all parameters passed unmodified. The pairing equation implementation is outside the scope of this Go codebase audit.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: No counterexample possible in the Go wrapper. The Go code cannot weaken entropy as it only converts types and delegates to the C library. The EIP-7594 spec requires hash_to_bls_field over all inputs with approximately 255-bit effective entropy.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: Attacker-controlled inputs (commitments, cellIndices, cells, proofs) are passed unmodified to the C library. The C library's Fiat-Shamir transcript binds all inputs before deriving r. Attacker cannot influence challenge derivation at the Go layer.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: The Go wrapper faithfully passes all four attacker-controlled inputs to the C library without modification. No partial input suppression or reordering occurs. The entropy properties are governed solely by the C library's EIP-7594 Fiat-Shamir implementation.

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: Entropy generation is an external library concern. The Go wrapper correctly passes all inputs including attacker-controlled ones to the library without weakening entropy.

audit_items.summary: Random challenge r generation is fully delegated to the c-kzg-4844 C library with approximately 255-bit entropy per EIP-7594. The Go wrapper introduces no entropy reduction.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: Array alignment invariant holds: consistent index i across all four arrays. Length pre-validation by VerifyDataColumnSidecar prevents misalignment. RLC/RLI/RLP internal computation is C library concern outside Go scope.

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Do actor-p2p-peer and actor-validator-node correctly invoke verify_cell_kzg_proof_batch_impl before accepting data column sidecars?

Both ultimately call peerdas.VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs -> kzg.VerifyCellKZGProofBatch. The seenDataColumn cache check occurs AFTER KZG verification, so caching cannot bypass verification.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: In validateDataColumn: inclusion proof is verified before KZG. In verifyDataColumnSidecarsByPeer: optimistic batch verify then per-peer fallback; failed peers are downscored. No path found where verification is skipped before sidecar acceptance.

Failed verification returns ValidationReject. Peer penalization via BadResponsesScorer.Increment is correctly applied.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: Invariant 'KZG verification precedes acceptance' holds in both paths. verifier.SatisfyRequirement(RequireSidecarKzgProofVerified) is called after batch validation success. No bypass through caching, deduplication, or early return was found.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_identified: validateWithKzgBatchVerifier with fallback to validateUnbatchedColumnsKzg; seenDataColumn cache post-verification

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: Verification is mandatory on both gossip and RPC paths with no bypass found. Peer penalization on invalid sidecars is correctly implemented.

audit_items.summary: KZG verification is mandatory on all data column sidecar reception paths. No bypass via caching, deduplication, or early exit was found. Batch failure correctly falls back to per-item verification. Peer penalization is correctly implemented.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: No hash_to_bls_field logic exists in the Go layer. The c-kzg-4844 library implements EIP-7594 which specifies SHA-256-based hash_to_bls_field with proper modular reduction per draft-irtf-cfrg-hash-to-curve. No counterexample in Go code.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: The c-kzg-4844 library is the standard Ethereum consensus implementation used across all major clients. The hash_to_bls_field entropy properties are standardized in EIP-7594. Not attacker-exploitable at the Go layer.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: The hash function properties are an external library invariant. No modifications to the hash input occur in the Go layer. audit_items.summary: hash_to_bls_field is fully implemented in the c-kzg-4844 C library per EIP-7594 with SHA-256-based uniform random field element generation. The Go layer introduces no entropy reduction.

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Is the random challenge r resistant to attacker influence through crafted P2P inputs?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: All attacker-controlled P2P inputs (cells, proofs, indices, commitments) flow through VerifyDataColumnsSidecarKZGProofs to the C library without intermediate processing that could enable challenge manipulation. The data path is fully linear and synchronous.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: All four input arrays are constructed from sidecar fields with no truncation, reordering, or pre-processing that could enable chosen-prefix attacks. SHA-256 preimage resistance prevents attacker from crafting inputs that produce a weak challenge.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: Challenge derivation occurs inside the C library's synchronous computation. No intermediate state is observable by the attacker. Rogue-key attacks are prevented by the inclusion proof requirement anchoring commitments to the proposer-signed block.

audit_items.title: Supporting Check: Can an attacker exploit weak entropy to forge proofs where invalid cells pass batch verification?

phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: The batch verification equation sum(r^i * verify_i) = 0 is computed entirely within c-kzg-4844. The Go layer has no influence over the entropy of r. The C library uses SHA-256-based hash_to_bls_field per EIP-7594 producing approximately 255 bits of effective entropy after modular reduction.

phase2_symbolic_execution.summary: A proof forgery attack requires finding inputs where sum(r^i * error_i) = 0 mod p. With approximately 255-bit entropy, the probability of random cancellation is approximately 2^(-255) per attempt, computationally infeasible. No reduced-entropy path exists in the Go layer.

phase2_5_reachability_analysis.summary: The Go code provides no mechanism to weaken the entropy of the challenge r. All computations including r_powers computation are internal to the C library. Full entropy (approximately 255 bits) is maintained.

phase3_invariant_proving.summary: Full entropy (approximately 255 bits) is maintained by the c-kzg-4844 library's Fiat-Shamir implementation. The Go wrapper cannot reduce this entropy. The soundness bound of (1 - 1/p) is a property of the C library's conformance to EIP-7594.
phase3_invariant_proving.guard_identified: EIP-7594 mandated hash_to_bls_field with full field-element entropy in C library

phase3_5_scope_filtering.reason: Entropy exhaustion attack is not feasible against a correctly implemented EIP-7594 library with approximately 255-bit challenge entropy. The Go wrapper introduces no entropy reduction.

audit_items.summary: Proof forgery via entropy exhaustion is computationally infeasible due to approximately 255-bit challenge entropy in the EIP-7594 compliant c-kzg-4844 library. The Go wrapper introduces no entropy reduction.
